title: Two consecutive edge loops recompute identical _resolve_submodel_endpoint results for every edge
description: The root_node_sources loop (1156-1183) and the root_connect_pairs loop (1195-1235) each iterate `for edge in edges` and independently compute actual_src = _resolve_submodel_endpoint(edge, src, sh, prefix='out__', ...) and actual_tgt = _resolve_submodel_endpoint(edge, tgt, th, prefix='in__', ...) with identical arguments, then derive src_func/tgt_func the same way (root_id_to_func.get(actual_*, _sanitize_func_name(actual_*))). The only difference is loop 1 filters to actual_tgt in root_node_ids and records sources, while loop 2 records connect pairs for all edges. The boundary resolution (which also re-raises on malformed handles) is therefore performed twice per edge. Merging into a single pass over edges that computes actual_src/actual_tgt/src_func/tgt_func once and feeds both root_node_sources/root_node_source_ids and root_connect_pairs would remove the duplicated resolution and the second identical raise-path.
evidence: Loop 1 lines 1163-1176 and Loop 2 lines 1202-1215 contain the same four _resolve_submodel_endpoint(...) calls with the same parameters; src_func/tgt_func derivation at 1181 and 1217-1218 is identical. Both loops read the same `edges` list with no mutation in between, so per-edge resolution is deterministic and recomputed.
behavior_preservation: Combining the two loops into one pass yields identical root_node_sources, root_node_source_ids and root_connect_pairs (same append order, same filter on root_node_ids for sources, no filter for connect pairs). _resolve_submodel_endpoint is pure and raises deterministically, so doing the resolution once per edge raises on exactly the same malformed edges at the same stage.
